name.en: Fake FCA: “we’ve recovered your lost money, just pay a fee”

how.en: Scammers pretend to be the FCA. Some say the FCA has recovered money from a crypto wallet opened in your name. Others target people who already lost money to a loan or investment scam and offer to get it back, or send emails saying you owe money after a court judgment. Each time, you are asked to pay or share sensitive details such as PINs and passwords. The FCA never asks you to transfer money to it.

text.en: You are contacted by phone, text, email or WhatsApp by someone saying they are from the FCA.
They say they have recovered money you lost, or that you owe money.
They ask for a fee or a payment to release the money or settle the debt.
They ask for your bank PINs or passwords.

Financial Conduct Authority: We have recovered funds from a cryptocurrency wallet registered in your name. To release the balance to you, a verification fee must be paid. Contact your case officer today.

en: fca called to recover my money
pay a fee to get lost money back
fake fca email county court judgment
company offered to recover my scam losses
fca asked for my bank pin
Anyone offering to recover money you lost, for a fee.
The FCA, or anyone, asking you to transfer money to them.
Don’t pay. The FCA never asks you to transfer money or for PINs and passwords.
If unsure, contact the FCA using details on its official website.
If you paid, call your bank and report it to Report Fraud.

sources.title: Almost 5,000 fake FCA scams reported in first 6 months of 2025
